statement: Single-stage, single-dimension KV compression methods hit an accuracy wall at high compression ratios, while two-stage, two-dimensional decomposition preserves accuracy much further. RocketKV shows that combining coarse permanent eviction (SnapKV) with fine dynamic two-dimensional top-k selection (HSA over sequence+head) reaches near-Exact-TopK accuracy at 256-token budgets (>400x compression on NIAH), whereas single-stage SnapKV/Quest/SparQ degrade sharply; the key observation is that unique Exact-TopK indices across decoding steps are far fewer than the sequence length, so evicting first makes the subsequent top-k prediction far easier.
